newsitem.title: CHINA: Central bankers end China meeting, statement seen.
newsitem.headline: Central bankers end China meeting, statement seen.

text.p: Asian central bankers on Friday wound up a one-day annual meeting in Shanghai widely believed to be focused on regional currency stability.
A news briefing and a statement were planned for about 5.30 p.m.(0930 GMT), officials said.
Approached by reporters as he emerged from the meeting, Hong Kong Monetary Authority chief executive Joseph Yam said: "I'm quite satisfied."
Other participants at the meeting said there would be further details in the news briefing.

The Shanghai conference of the Executives' Meeting of East Asia and Pacific Central Banks followed weeks of speculative attacks on several Asian currencies, most notably the Thai baht, which has lost about 20 percent since it was allowed to float on July 2.
Some market analysts have looked to the meeting to provide some form of statement on regional central bank cooperation to help defend some of the weaker currencies.
Other analysts, however, have said some central banks may be reluctant to commit their foreign exchange reserves in the defence of these currencies.
